title: Covariant return types
answer: A covariant return type allows an overriding method to return a more specific reference type than the method in its superclass or interface, provided that return type is a subtype of the original return type. Parameter types still must match the overriding signature. Covariant returns improve usability because callers of the subclass can receive the more specific type without casting while preserving substitutability through the parent contract.
